author: architecture-closer

rejectedPredecessor.retainedWhy: v5 remains historical evidence. Its sealed-versus-effective split survives review and is carried forward; its closure, concurrency, lineage, D9 and authority claims did not.

repairedElsewhere.R3-RTV5-01: artifacts/evaluation-proof.v1.json + artifacts/check-evaluation-proof.py — the proof object graph is a separate versioned binding rather than an overload of retention.

role: Decide what happens to a sealed authoritative Run when its evidence stops being available: which units its capability depends on, how a reader and a purger serialize, what targeted purge can honestly promise, and which typed outcome each failure produces.

carriedForwardFromV5.sealedVersusEffective: A Run seals one immutable assurance capability and evidence inventory. Readers DERIVE an effective capability from live unit states. The sealed value is never rewritten.
carriedForwardFromV5.why: Reviewer-3 explicitly endorsed this split and directed repair toward its closure and operational semantics rather than a return to tiers or Run rewriting.

capabilityLattice.authorityFloor: An authoritative gate, baseline mutation, waiver decision, or compliance assertion requires effective capability >= verifiable.

unitStates.meaning: replay closure object not obtainable offline

carriedForwardFromV5.terminalMonotonicity: The terminally lost set is append-only. A terminal state never returns to AVAILABLE. OUTAGE may recover, so effective capability can dip and recover under transient loss while the terminal ceiling is non-increasing.

capabilityClosure.problem: v5 derived effective capability from whatever units a caller happened to list. Omitting or misclassifying one proof dependency left effectiveCapability at verifiable after the material needed to verify was gone (R3-RTV5-CE-03).
capabilityClosure.rule: The sealed Run carries a host-owned capability-requirement closure that maps EVERY reference in the evaluation-proof graph to exactly one retention unit, with the minimum capability that needs it. The closure is recomputed and verified at seal time and at read time.

derivation.source: artifacts/evaluation-proof.v1.json proof graph for the Run
derivation.requiredForCapability: the MINIMUM lattice level of any proof that references the object. A reference used by a verifiable no-match is 'verifiable' even if a replay closure also uses it.
derivation.member: unitId || 0x1F || requiredForCapability || 0x1F || sorted objectRefs joined by 0x1E

invariantsEnforced: every proof reference maps to exactly one unit — no omission
no two units alias the same object reference — no duplicate that could mask a purge
no unit declares a capability weaker than the strongest claim depending on it — no downgrade
the closure commitment recomputes from the units
a unit is available only if EVERY object it contains is available — partial availability retains no authority

fixtures.why: one verifiable unit purged demotes to recorded
losing only the replay closure demotes replayable -> verifiable
R3-RTV5-CE-03: the closure omits the predicate-semantics unit
two units alias the same object, so a purge of one is masked
R3-RTV5-CE-03: predicate unit downgraded to replayable while a verifiable no-match needs it
closure commitment does not recompute from the units
a unit is partially available and still counted as available

leaseProtocol.problem: v5 used a boolean resolvedAtAdmission. A second one-shot process holding the purge authority could delete a unit between resolution and use (R3-RTV5-CE-04). One-shot topology does not remove cross-process concurrency.

operation.name: resolve-and-pin
operation.atomicity: ONE transaction in the project ledger. Resolving effective capability and acquiring the read lease are not separable steps.
operation.durableRecord: projects/<ProjectId>/ledger.sqlite — the same transactional authority that owns the purge lease, so both serialize in one lock domain

leaseRecord.note: leaseId is durable and content-independent; a boolean is never a lease.

leaseProtocol.totalOrder: Ledger sequence numbers order read leases and purge leases in one domain. There is no separate read-side lock that a purge could miss.

transitions.scenario: read lease HELD, purge targets a covered unit
transitions.resolution: purge is REJECTED, not queued; it reports the blocking leaseIds
transitions.why: contention is retryable; the caller re-runs purge after the reader finishes. Waiting would let a long reader block deletion indefinitely, which is a privacy hazard.

transitions.scenario: purge committed (unit tombstoned), then resolve-and-pin requested
transitions.resolution: lease acquisition fails for that unit; effective capability is recomputed without it
transitions.outcome: request-rejected / REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE when the caller required authoritative use
transitions.why: the evidence is terminally gone; restating or re-running is the remedy

transitions.scenario: PURGE-PREPARED tombstone exists but physical removal has not run
transitions.resolution: resolve-and-pin refuses the unit — a prepared purge is already authoritative intent
transitions.why: TM deletionProtocol resumes tombstoned purges on startup before analysis; granting a lease over prepared material would resurrect it

transitions.resolution: lease is RECLAIMED-STALE once expiresAtSeq passes and the liveness token is dead; units return to normal purge eligibility
transitions.outcome: no user-visible outcome; recovery is internal
transitions.why: a crashed reader must not pin evidence forever

transitions.scenario: retention expiry falls due while a read lease is HELD
transitions.resolution: expiry does not preempt a live lease; it applies at release
transitions.why: an admitted, pinned read completes against the state it was admitted on — this is the actual TOCTOU closure

transitions.scenario: resolve-and-pin retried with the same leaseId
transitions.resolution: idempotent — returns the same grant and does not extend the pin window

leaseProtocol.doesNotClaim: Runtime atomicity is a property of the ledger transaction, not of this document. This contract specifies the required serialization; it does not demonstrate an implementation achieves it.

fixtures.scenario: purge attempted while a read lease is HELD
fixtures.why: contention is retryable; purge is rejected rather than queued

fixtures.scenario: purge committed before admission; authoritative use requested

fixtures.why: a prepared purge is authoritative intent; a lease must not resurrect it
a crashed reader must not pin evidence forever

fixtures.scenario: retention expiry falls due during a held lease
fixtures.why: expiry applies at release; the admitted read completes — this is the TOCTOU closure

fixtures.scenario: resolve-and-pin retried with the same leaseId
fixtures.why: retry safety without extending the pin window

storageAndLineage.problem: v5 promised that a targeted purge affects exactly the units containing the material AND leaves unrelated Runs untouched AND never rewrites sealed identity. R3-RTV5-CE-05 showed those three cannot all hold when a fact partition holds many subjects and is shared by many Runs.
storageAndLineage.resolution: The over-promise is withdrawn. The purge key is the content-addressed OBJECT, not the subject, and blocked material is reported rather than silently removed or silently retained.

join.crossProject: physical deduplication is FORBIDDEN; equal content in two projects is two independently written files
join.withinProject: shared objects use transactional reference counts plus a reachability proof

storageAndLineage.purgeKeyGranularity: content-addressed object within one ProjectId namespace

targetedPurgeSemantics.step1: resolve the selection (path/subject/privacy class) to the exact set of objects containing it, via proof-unit -> object -> Run reachability in that project's ledger
targetedPurgeSemantics.step2: partition those objects into UNBLOCKED (reachable only by Runs in the purge scope) and BLOCKED (reachable by a retained Run outside the scope)
targetedPurgeSemantics.step3: tombstone and remove UNBLOCKED objects; report BLOCKED objects as retained with their blocking Run IDs
targetedPurgeSemantics.step4: append an audit record with before/after inventory commitments
targetedPurgeSemantics.honestPromise: A targeted purge removes exactly the unblocked objects containing the selection. It does NOT guarantee the selected subject is gone — shared retained material is reported, never silently removed and never silently ignored.
targetedPurgeSemantics.escalation: Removing blocked material requires explicitly purging every blocking Run. That is a separate, stronger operation the user must request; it is not implied by a targeted purge.
targetedPurgeSemantics.noSilentDemotion: Because BLOCKED objects are never removed, a targeted purge never demotes a Run outside its scope. Runs inside the scope demote to the capability their surviving units support.
targetedPurgeSemantics.noIdentityRewrite: Objects are never rewritten in place. A shared partition is retained or removed whole; editing it would change an identity two sealed Runs already committed to.

storageAndLineage.residual: Subject-level isolation inside a shared partition is NOT provided. If product requires that a targeted purge always removes the subject, the storage architecture must supply subject-isolated partitioning or per-Run duplication, both of which have cost and privacy consequences that are not decided here.

fixtures.why: unshared object containing the subject is removed
R3-RTV5-CE-05: shared partition is reported blocked, not removed
mixed: one removable, one blocked; no out-of-scope demotion either way
objects not containing the subject are untouched

d9Derivation.problem: v5's RC-10 checked only that a code was in D9's closed vocabulary. R3-PROBE-04 changed a row's class while keeping the code and the checker passed. v5 also mapped recoverable OUTAGE to the same code as terminal purge, erasing the remedy distinction D9 groups by (R3-RTV5-CE-06).
d9Derivation.rule: Every row declares complete D9 scenario axes. The retained checker imports the live d9 reference derivation (check_d9.derive_class / derive_codes, which d9-exit-contract.v1.6 names as referenceDerivation.implementation) and asserts the declared class and code are what D9 DERIVES. Membership is not derivation.

rows.situation: authoritative use of a Run whose required unit is terminally PURGED or EXPIRED
required unit is in transient OUTAGE — unmounted or removable store
rows.whyNotUnsatisfiable: The same request becomes satisfiable when the store returns. D9 groups codes by remedy: remount and retry is not restate-or-re-run.

rows.situation: ledger integrity failure while resolving evidence
content-addressed proof object cannot be linked or materialised
rows.whyNotLedgerCorrupt: Object materialisation failure has its own remedy — run store repair — and D9 already separates it.

rows.situation: addressed Run was retention-collected and a tombstone is retained
purge rejected because a read lease covers the targeted unit (LP-1)
rows.whyRetryable: Contention, not corruption. The purge succeeds once the reader releases.

rows.situation: caller requires complete evidence a degraded Run cannot supply
rows.whyIncluded: R3-RTV5-05 named this as the omitted D9 case. An admitted completeness query is answered honestly as indeterminate, not rejected.

rows.situation: durable or authoritative evidence requested with no explicit retention policy resolved

requiredDistinctions.why: R3-RTV5-05 named the exact distinctions the mapping must keep separate. Listing them makes coverage checkable, so a row cannot be quietly dropped and leave a whole remedy class unrepresented.

byCode.REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE: terminal authorized loss (purge/expiry) and unsatisfiable durable request
byCode.HOST.IO_FAILURE: transient storage or provider outage — recoverable
byCode.CAS.LINK_FAILED: content-addressed object cannot be materialised — store repair
byCode.QUERY.COMPLETENESS_UNMET: admitted completeness query answered as indeterminate

requiredDistinctions.requiresSuccessRow: at least one row must terminate success, or honest inspection of degraded history has been lost

custodyPolicy.perObligation: Custody strategy — frozen evidence or an exact deterministic regeneration closure — is selected per proof obligation by the host, never by a producer.

recommendedDefaultPosture.recommendation: no managed durable user-derived write without an explicit project storage and retention policy
recommendedDefaultPosture.whenPolicyMissing: the request is explicitly advisory/ephemeral, or rejected if durable or authoritative evidence was requested (RD-10)
recommendedDefaultPosture.selfSignoffPolicy: This architecture candidate RECOMMENDS the posture and states its consequences. It does not and cannot record product acceptance. v5 asserted PRODUCT-SIGNED-OFF inside its own status field, which was an authority inversion (R3-RTV5-06).
consequencesIfAccepted: a first Run with no configured policy cannot produce durable authoritative evidence
CI and agents must carry a pre-provisioned or versioned policy
no interactive consent question is answered implicitly by a non-interactive client
consequencesIfReplaced: a documented short default retention with first-run consent would need an explicit consent mechanism and a real purge path
the storage admission checks in RA-6/E6 still apply before the first durable write

integrationState.rule: This candidate closes NOTHING outside its own artifact. Every cross-artifact state below stays as it is until independent re-review passes, product records CD-RT-5, and one serialized integration lands.

pending.note: v5 set it RESOLVED and cited a path that did not exist. That edit is superseded; see integrationPatch in the adjudication artifact.
only the product authority may change this
narrative reconciliation is part of the serialized integration

invariants.assert: The sealed assurance capability and sealed evidence inventory are immutable; no availability event rewrites them.
Effective capability is derived at read time from the sealed closure and live unit states, and is never persisted into the sealed Run.
Effective capability never exceeds sealed capability, and terminal loss is irreversible.
A Run whose effective capability is below verifiable is never accepted as an authoritative input.
Effective capability and the read lease are acquired in one atomic durable operation ordered against purge in a single lock domain.
A degradation report identifies each unavailable unit and its cause; one Run-wide word is insufficient.
Inspecting a degraded Run succeeds and reports honestly; loss of proof restricts authority, never readability.
Purge is explicit and recorded and never converts an unverifiable claim into a trusted one.
No managed durable user-derived write occurs without an explicit resolved retention policy.
Every outcome DERIVES from D9's live reference derivation over complete axes; vocabulary membership alone is not conformance.
The capability-requirement closure is exact: every proof reference maps to exactly one unit at the minimum capability that needs it, with no omission, alias, or downgrade.
A unit is available only if every object it contains is available; partial availability retains no authority.
A targeted purge removes only unblocked objects and reports blocked objects with their blocking Run IDs; it never demotes a Run outside its scope and never rewrites a shared object.
This candidate never records product acceptance for CD-RT-5 and never declares a cross-artifact dependency closed.

assurance.why: A contract plus a retained checker is design-integrity evidence. AS-1: implementable:true performs no assurance transition. Nothing here is QUALIFIED or DEMONSTRATED and no product gate is unblocked.

retainedResiduals.statement: No-match fold plus reverification cost including retained fact custody is unmeasured. No constant-size or orders-of-magnitude claim is authorized.
retainedResiduals.doesNotBlock: implementing the proof or custody model

retainedResiduals.statement: Subject-level isolation inside a shared fact partition is not provided. Targeted purge reports blocked shared material rather than removing it.
Real deletion for deduplicated and backup-held objects remains open; purge promises an honest recorded transition, not forensic erasure.

v6 and its checkers are authored by the same agent that authored the rejected v5. Independent re-review by an agent that authored neither the proof contract nor the checkers is required before any seal.
CD-RT-5 remains BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A. Product authority must accept or replace the recommended default posture.
Storage exposure detector coverage remains catalog-scoped with DETECTED/NOT-DETECTED/UNKNOWN fallback.

knownLimitations: Same-author risk is the dominant residual: the agent that wrote the rejected v5 wrote v6, the proof contract, and all three checkers. Green checkers here are checker-scope evidence only, exactly as reviewer-3 recorded.
The lease protocol specifies required serialization. It is not demonstrated against a real ledger, and no crash-injection harness exists.
The storage join reads the admission-storage lane's adjudication at a point in time. If that lane changes purge or reference-count semantics, the targeted-purge rules here must be re-derived.
Effective-capability derivation is specified as a pure function over unit states. Its cost for a Run with many thousands of units is unmeasured.
The D9 rows are validated against the live derivation, but they enumerate the situations this contract knows about. Totality over all future operations is not proved.
confidence: high on the sealed/effective split and the D9 derivation join; medium-high on the closure and lease specifications, which are exact but unexecuted; medium on targeted purge, which is now honest but delivers less than v5 promised.
sealRecommendation: DO NOT SEAL. Hand to an independent reviewer who authored neither the proof contract nor the checkers. Phase 1A closes only after that review passes and product records CD-RT-5.
